name: The Nines
positioning: The Nines, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Portland: an art-filled hotel on the top nine floors of the historic Meier and Frank Building in downtown Portland
best_for: Art and design lovers who want local Oregon artwork throughout the hotel
City travelers who want a downtown base near Pioneer Courthouse Square and the MAX light rail

facts.text: Meier & Frank established their flagship store and headquarters in Portland in 1909.
The name The Nines pays homage to the building's roots as a beacon of 'dressed to the nines' fashion.
The lobby, restaurants and library include works by local artists such as Melody Owen, Matt McCormick and Gus Van Sant, along with a 35-foot LED chandelier.
The hotel's art collection was curated by former Andy Warhol associate Paige Powell.
Rooms feature satin drapes, velvet recamiers and robin blue pillows.
Rooms have Frette linens, a marble tub and local Beekind bath amenities.
Suites provide electric fireplaces, Club Lounge access and views of downtown Portland.
The signature Nines Suite has 9-foot ceilings and oversized windows with city views.
The hotel library has a full-size billiards table beneath an antler chandelier, leather sofas and hundreds of books.
The hotel is in downtown Portland near Pioneer Courthouse Square, steps from tax-free shopping at Pioneer Place.
The hotel sits directly on the MAX light rail line, five stops from Washington Park.
Urban Farmer Steakhouse is situated within The Nines' living room.

highlights.text: The Nines occupies the top nine floors of the historic Meier and Frank Building in downtown Portland.
The Nines has curated a collection of more than 400 pieces of local Oregon artwork, including sculptures, paintings and custom installations.
Each guest room features a one-of-a-kind monotype silkscreen created by a student at the Pacific Northwest College of Art.
A seven-story light-filled atrium was created to showcase city views, while the building's original exterior was retained.
Departure Restaurant + Lounge has two rooftop patios overlooking downtown from the top floor of the Meier & Frank building.

considerations.text: Rooms do not have a fridge.
A daily destination amenity fee applies.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may bring typical city noise.
